mishnayos.summary: When two pairs of witnesses watch from two windows, whether they count as one group or two depends on whether they can see each other. Rabbi Yosei says the witnesses themselves must warn the sinner, and Beis Din must hear witnesses directly, not through a translator.

chunks.he: הָיוּ שְׁנַיִם רוֹאִין אוֹתוֹ מֵחַלּוֹן זֶה
chunks.en: If two people were watching him from this window
chunks.st: In a case where there were two witnesses observing an individual violating a capital transgression from this window in a house,

chunks.en: and two were watching him from that window,
chunks.st: and two observing him from that window in a house,

chunks.en: and one person in the middle was warning him,
chunks.st: and one person was forewarning the transgressor in the middle between the two sets of witnesses,
chunks.stMore: the halakha depends on the circumstances.

chunks.he: בִּזְמַן שֶׁמִּקְצָתָן רוֹאִין אֵלּוּ אֶת אֵלּוּ,
chunks.en: if some of them can see each other,
chunks.st: In a situation where some of the witnesses observing from the two windows see each other,

chunks.en: then they are one testimony.
chunks.st: the testimony of all these witnesses constitutes one testimony,

chunks.en: But if not,
chunks.st: but if they do not see each other,

chunks.en: they are two separate testimonies.
chunks.st: the testimony of these witnesses constitutes two independent testimonies.

chunks.he: לְפִיכָךְ אִם נִמְצֵאת אַחַת מֵהֶן זוֹמֶמֶת,
chunks.en: So if one group is found to be zomemin,
chunks.st: Therefore, as two independent sets of witnesses, if one of the sets was found to be a set of conspiring witnesses,
chunks.stMore: while the testimony of the other set remained valid,

words.note: Proven to be plotting, false witnesses.

chunks.en: the sinner and the zomemin are put to death, and the second group is free.
chunks.st: both he, the one accused of violating the capital transgression, and they, the conspiring witnesses, are executed, and the second set, whose testimony remained valid, is exempt.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: Someone is never put to death
chunks.st: Transgressors are never executed

chunks.he: עַד שֶׁיְּהוּ פִּי שְׁנֵי עֵדָיו מַתְרִין בּוֹ,
chunks.en: unless his two witnesses are the ones who warn him,
chunks.st: unless his two witnesses are the ones forewarning him,

chunks.he: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דברים יז) עַל פִּי שְׁנַיִם עֵדִים.
chunks.en: as it says, "By the word of two witnesses."
chunks.st: as it is stated: “At the mouth of two witnesses
chunks.stMore: …he who is to be put to death shall die” (Deuteronomy 17:6), from which it is derived that it is from the mouths of the two witnesses that the accused must be forewarned, and forewarning issued by someone else is insufficient.

chunks.en: Another explanation:
chunks.st: Alternatively,

chunks.en: "By the word of two witnesses"
chunks.st: from the phrase “at the mouth of two witnesses”

chunks.he: שֶׁלֹּא תְהֵא סַנְהֶדְרִין שׁוֹמַעַת מִפִּי הַתֻּרְגְּמָן:
chunks.en: means the Sanhedrin may not hear the witnesses through a translator.
chunks.explain: The judges must hear the witnesses' own words.
chunks.st: one derives that the judges must hear the testimony directly from the witnesses, and the Sanhedrin will not hear testimony from the mouth of an interpreter.

words.note: The great Beis Din of seventy-one judges.

mishnayos.summary: Someone whose case was decided by Beis Din cannot run away to escape it. The Sanhedrin was so careful that putting someone to death was very rare; the mishnah tells how rare it should be.

chunks.en: Someone whose judgment was decided, and he ran away,
chunks.st: one whose verdict was delivered and he was sentenced to death and he fled,

chunks.en: and then came before the same Beis Din,
chunks.st: and he then came before the same court that sentenced him,

chunks.en: we do not undo his judgment.
chunks.st: they do not overturn his verdict and retry him.
chunks.stMore: Rather, the court administers the previous verdict.

chunks.en: Anywhere that two witnesses stand up and say,
chunks.st: Consequently, in any place where two witnesses will stand and say:

chunks.en: "We testify about a certain man
chunks.st: We testify with regard to a man called so-and-so

chunks.he: שֶׁנִּגְמַר דִּינוֹ בְּבֵית דִּינוֹ שֶׁל פְּלוֹנִי,
chunks.en: that his judgment was decided in the Beis Din of so-and-so,
chunks.st: that his verdict was delivered and he was sentenced to death in the court of so-and-so,

chunks.en: and so-and-so and so-and-so were his witnesses,"
chunks.st: and so-and-so and so-and-so were his witnesses,

chunks.en: then he is put to death.
chunks.st: that person shall be executed on the basis of that testimony.

chunks.en: A Sanhedrin works both in Eretz Yisrael and outside Eretz Yisrael.
chunks.st: The mishna continues: The mitzva to establish a Sanhedrin with the authority to administer capital punishments is in effect both in Eretz Yisrael and outside Eretz Yisrael.

chunks.he: סַנְהֶדְרִין הַהוֹרֶגֶת אֶחָד בְּשָׁבוּעַ נִקְרֵאת חָבְלָנִית.
chunks.en: A Sanhedrin that puts someone to death once in seven years is called a destructive Sanhedrin.
chunks.explain: They checked so carefully that it almost never happened.
chunks.st: A Sanhedrin that executes a transgressor once in seven years is characterized as a destructive tribunal.
chunks.stMore: Since the Sanhedrin would subject the testimony to exacting scrutiny, it was extremely rare for a defendant to be executed.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:

chunks.en: even once in seventy years.
chunks.st: This categorization applies to a Sanhedrin that executes a transgressor once in seventy years.

chunks.en: Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva say,
chunks.st: Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva say:

chunks.en: If we had been in the Sanhedrin,
chunks.st: If we had been members of the Sanhedrin,

chunks.en: no person would ever have been put to death.
chunks.st: we would have conducted trials in a manner whereby no person would have ever been executed.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.he: אַף הֵן מַרְבִּין שׁוֹפְכֵי דָמִים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל:
chunks.en: Then they would also make more murderers among the Jewish people.
chunks.explain: People would not be afraid of being punished.
chunks.st: In adopting that approach, they too would increase the number of murderers among the Jewish people.
chunks.stMore: The death penalty would lose its deterrent value, as all potential murderers would know that no one is ever executed.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who kills a person by accident must go into galus, to a city of refuge. This mishnah teaches the rule: if it happened while something was moving downward, he goes into galus; if not, he does not.

chunks.en: These are the people who go into galus:
chunks.explain: Galus means going to live in a city of refuge.
chunks.st: These are the people who are exiled:

chunks.en: someone who kills a person by accident.
chunks.st: Anyone who kills a person unintentionally.
chunks.stMore: Whether one is liable to be exiled depends on the particular circumstances of the case:

chunks.he: הָיָה מְעַגֵּל בְּמַעְגִּילָה וְנָפְלָה עָלָיו וַהֲרָגַתּוּ,
chunks.en: If he was rolling a roller on his roof, and it fell on someone and killed him,
chunks.explain: A heavy roller was used to smooth a roof.
chunks.st: If one was rolling a roller to smooth the covering of mortar that he applied to seal his roof and the roller fell upon a person and killed him,

chunks.he: הָיָה מְשַׁלְשֵׁל בְּחָבִית וְנָפְלָה עָלָיו וַהֲרָגַתּוּ,
chunks.en: or he was lowering a barrel, and it fell on someone and killed him,
chunks.st: or if one was lowering a barrel from the roof and it fell on a person and killed him,

chunks.he: הָיָה יוֹרֵד בְּסֻלָּם וְנָפַל עָלָיו וַהֲרָגוֹ,
chunks.en: or he was going down a ladder, and he fell on someone and killed him,
chunks.st: or if he was descending a ladder and he fell on a person and killed him,

chunks.en: he goes into galus.
chunks.st: in all of these cases, he is exiled.

chunks.en: But if he was pulling a roller toward himself,
chunks.st: But if one was pulling a roller toward him

chunks.en: and it fell on someone and killed him,
chunks.st: and it fell from his hands upon a person and killed him,

chunks.en: or he was pulling up a barrel,
chunks.st: or if one was lifting a barrel

chunks.en: and the rope tore and it fell on someone and killed him,
chunks.st: and the rope was severed and it fell upon a person and killed him,

chunks.he: הָיָה עוֹלֶה בְסֻלָּם וְנָפַל עָלָיו וַהֲרָגוֹ,
chunks.en: or he was climbing up a ladder, and he fell on someone and killed him,
chunks.st: or if one was climbing a ladder and he fell upon a person and killed him,

chunks.en: he does not go into galus.
chunks.st: that unintentional murderer is not exiled.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.en: Whenever it happened while moving downward,
chunks.st: Any murderer who kills unintentionally through his downward

chunks.en: he goes into galus.
chunks.st: motion is exiled,

chunks.en: And when it was not while moving downward,
chunks.st: and one who kills not through his downward

chunks.en: he does not go into galus.
chunks.st: motion is not exiled.

chunks.en: If the iron head of an ax slipped off its handle and killed someone,
chunks.st: If the blade of an ax or hatchet was displaced from its handle, and it flew through the air and killed a person,

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says:

chunks.en: he does not go into galus.
chunks.st: He is not exiled,

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: and the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: he goes into galus.
chunks.st: He is exiled.

chunks.en: If a piece of wood flew off a log being chopped and killed someone,
chunks.st: If part of a tree that is being split flew through the air and killed a person,

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says:

chunks.en: he goes into galus.
chunks.st: The murderer is exiled,

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: and the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: he does not go into galus.
chunks.st: He is not exiled.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who throws a stone and kills by accident goes into galus only if the person was allowed to be in that place. Abba Shaul adds that someone doing a mitzvah, like a father teaching his son, does not go into galus.

chunks.en: Someone who threw a stone into a public place and killed someone
chunks.st: One who threw a stone into the public domain and killed

chunks.en: goes into galus.
chunks.st: a person is exiled.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov says:

chunks.en: If after the stone left his hand,
chunks.st: If after the stone left his hand

chunks.en: the other person stuck out his head and got hit,
chunks.st: the other person placed his head out into the public domain and received a blow from the stone,

chunks.en: he is free.
chunks.explain: When he threw it, nobody was there.
chunks.st: he is exempt,
chunks.stMore: as when he cast the stone into the public domain there was no one there.

chunks.en: If he threw a stone into his own courtyard and killed someone,
chunks.st: In the case of one who threw the stone into his courtyard and killed a person,

chunks.he: אִם יֵשׁ רְשׁוּת לַנִּזָּק לִכָּנֵס לְשָׁם,
chunks.en: if the person who got hurt was allowed to go in there,
chunks.st: if the victim had permission to enter into there,

chunks.en: he goes into galus.
chunks.st: the murderer is exiled,

chunks.en: But if not,
chunks.st: but if not,

chunks.en: he does not go into galus,
chunks.st: he is not exiled,

chunks.en: as it says, "And someone who goes
chunks.st: as it is stated with regard to the cities of refuge: “And as one

chunks.en: with his friend into the forest."
chunks.st: who goes with his neighbor into the forest” (Deuteronomy 19:5),
chunks.stMore: from which it is derived:

chunks.en: Just as the forest is a place where the one who gets hurt
chunks.st: Just as with regard to a forest, the victim

chunks.en: and the one who hurts are both allowed to go in,
chunks.st: and the assailant both have equal permission to enter there,
chunks.stMore: so too, with regard to all places that the victim and the assailant have permission to enter there, the killer is liable.

chunks.en: this leaves out a homeowner's courtyard,
chunks.st: This serves to exclude the courtyard of the homeowner,

chunks.he: שֶׁאֵין רְשׁוּת לַנִּזָּק וְלַמַּזִּיק לִכָּנֵס לְשָׁם.
chunks.en: where the one who gets hurt and the one who hurts are not both allowed to go in.
chunks.st: where the victim and the assailant do not both have permission to enter there.
chunks.stMore: Since the victim had no right to enter his courtyard, the unintentional murderer is exempt from exile.

chunks.en: Abba Shaul says,
chunks.st: Abba Shaul says:
chunks.stMore: Another halakha can be derived from that verse:

chunks.en: Just as chopping wood is something a person chooses to do,
chunks.explain: Galus is only when he did not have to be doing it.
chunks.st: Just as the cutting of wood that is mentioned in the verse is optional,
chunks.stMore: so too, all those liable to be exiled are examples of cases where the unintentional murderer was engaged in an activity that is optional.

chunks.en: this leaves out a father who hits his son to teach him,
chunks.st: This serves to exclude a father who strikes his son,

chunks.en: and a teacher who hits his student,
chunks.st: and a teacher who oppresses his student,

chunks.en: and the messenger of Beis Din who gives lashes.
chunks.st: and an agent of the court deputized to flog transgressors.
chunks.stMore: If, in the course of performing the mitzva with which they are charged, they unintentionally murdered the son, the student, or the person being flogged, respectively, they are exempt.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches who goes into galus for killing whom by accident. Someone who hated the person he killed usually does not go into galus, because it may not have been an accident.

chunks.en: A father goes into galus because of his son,
chunks.st: The father is exiled to a city of refuge due to his unintentional murder of his son.

chunks.en: and a son goes into galus because of his father.
chunks.st: And the son is exiled due to his unintentional murder of his father.

chunks.en: Everyone goes into galus because of a Jew,
chunks.st: Everyone is exiled due to their unintentional murder of a Jew,

chunks.en: and a Jew goes into galus because of any of them,
chunks.st: and a Jew is exiled due to his unintentional murder of any of them,

chunks.en: except because of a ger toshav.
chunks.explain: A non-Jew living in Eretz Yisrael who keeps the seven mitzvos of Noach.
chunks.st: except for the unintentional murder of a gentile who resides in Eretz Yisrael and observes the seven Noahide mitzvot [ger toshav].

chunks.en: And a ger toshav goes into galus only
chunks.st: And a ger toshav is exiled only

chunks.en: because of a ger toshav.
chunks.st: due to his unintentional murder of a ger toshav.

chunks.en: A blind person does not go into galus.
chunks.st: A blind person who unintentionally murdered another is not exiled;

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: he goes into galus.
chunks.st: He is exiled.

chunks.en: Someone who hated the person does not go into galus.
chunks.st: The enemy of the victim is not exiled,
chunks.stMore: as presumably it was not a completely unintentional act.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: The one who hated him is put to death,
chunks.st: Not only is an enemy not exiled, but he is executed by the court,

chunks.en: because he is like someone who was warned.
chunks.explain: He probably did it on purpose.
chunks.st: because his halakhic status is like that of one who is forewarned by witnesses
chunks.stMore: not to perform the action, as presumably he performed the action intentionally.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: There is an enemy who goes into galus,
chunks.st: There is an enemy who is exiled

chunks.en: and there is an enemy who does not go into galus.
chunks.st: and there is an enemy who is not exiled.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.he: כֹּל שֶׁהוּא יָכוֹל לוֹמַר לְדַעַת הָרַג,
chunks.en: Whenever one could say he killed on purpose,
chunks.st: In any case where an observer could say he killed knowingly,
chunks.stMore: where circumstances lead to the assumption that it was an intentional act,

chunks.en: he does not go into galus.
chunks.st: the enemy is not exiled,
chunks.stMore: even if he claims that he acted unintentionally.

chunks.en: But if he clearly killed without meaning to,
chunks.st: And if it is clear that he killed unknowingly,
chunks.stMore: as circumstances indicate that he acted unintentionally,

chunks.en: he goes into galus.
chunks.st: he is exiled, even though the victim is his enemy.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who killed by accident goes to one of the six cities of refuge: three across the Yarden and three in Eretz Yisrael. The cities only started working once all six were chosen.

chunks.en: Where do they go into galus?
chunks.st: To where are the unintentional murderers exiled?

chunks.en: To the cities of refuge:
chunks.explain: Special cities where he is safe from the relatives of the one he killed.
chunks.st: They are exiled to cities of refuge,

chunks.he: לַשָּׁלשׁ שֶׁבְּעֵבֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן וְלַשָּׁלשׁ שֶׁבְּאֶרֶץ כְּנַעַן,
chunks.en: to the three across the Yarden and the three in the land of Canaan,
chunks.st: to three cities that were in the east bank of the Jordan and to three cities that were in the land of Canaan,
chunks.stMore: i.e., Eretz Yisrael,

words.en: that are in the land of

chunks.en: as it says, "Three cities

chunks.en: you shall give across the Yarden, and three cities
chunks.st: shall you give beyond the Jordan and three cities

chunks.en: you shall give in the land of Canaan."
chunks.st: shall you give in the land of Canaan; they shall be cities of refuge” (Numbers 35:14).
chunks.stMore: The mishna comments:

chunks.he: עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִבְחֲרוּ שָׁלשׁ שֶׁבְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
chunks.en: Until the three in Eretz Yisrael were chosen,
chunks.st: Until the three cities of refuge that were in Eretz Yisrael were selected,

words.en: that are in the land of

chunks.he: לֹא הָיוּ שָׁלשׁ שֶׁבְּעֵבֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן קוֹלְטוֹת,
chunks.en: the three across the Yarden did not take anyone in,
chunks.st: an unintentional murderer would not be admitted to the three that were in the east bank of the Jordan,
chunks.stMore: even though the latter three were already selected by Moses (see Deuteronomy 4:41),

chunks.en: as it says, "Six cities of refuge shall there be,"
chunks.st: as it is stated: “Six cities of refuge shall they be” (Numbers 35:13),

chunks.en: so they work only when all six take people in together.
chunks.st: from which it is derived that they do not become cities of refuge until all six of them admit unintentional murderers as one.

mishnayos.summary: Straight roads were made to the cities of refuge. Two Torah scholars went with the one running there, to talk to the angry relative so he would not hurt him.

chunks.en: And roads were made straight for them from one city to another,
chunks.st: And roads were aligned for them from this city, i.e., all cities, to that city,
chunks.stMore: i.e., they would pave and straighten the access roads to the cities of refuge,

chunks.en: as it says, "Prepare for yourself
chunks.st: as it is stated: “Prepare for you

chunks.en: the road, and divide your land in three."
chunks.st: the road, and divide the borders of your land, which the Lord your God causes you to inherit, into three parts, that every murderer may flee there” (Deuteronomy 19:3).

words.en: and you shall divide in three

chunks.en: And they send two Torah scholars with him,
chunks.st: And the court would provide the unintentional murderers fleeing to a city of refuge with two Torah scholars,

chunks.en: in case the relative of the one who was killed tries to kill him on the way,
chunks.st: due to the concern that perhaps the blood redeemer, i.e., a relative of the murder victim seeking to avenge his death, will seek to kill him in transit,

chunks.st: and in that case they, the scholars, will talk to the blood redeemer

mishnayos.summary: Anyone who killed would first run to a city of refuge, and Beis Din would bring him back for judgment. One who must go into galus stays there until the Kohen Gadol dies.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says:

chunks.st: Initially, either one who killed another unintentionally

chunks.st: the court would execute him,

chunks.en: One who did not deserve death,
chunks.st: and for one who was not found liable to receive the death penalty, e.g., if they deemed that the death occurred due to circumstances beyond his control,

chunks.en: they let him go.
chunks.st: they would free him.

chunks.en: One who had to go into galus,
chunks.st: For one who was found liable to be exiled,

chunks.en: they bring him back to his place there,
chunks.st: the court would restore him to his place in the city of refuge,

chunks.en: as it says, "And they shall bring him back,
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And the congregation shall judge between the murderer and the blood redeemer…and the congregation shall restore him

chunks.en: the congregation, to his city of refuge."
chunks.st: to his city of refuge,
chunks.stMore: that he fled there” (Numbers 35:24–25), indicating that he had been in a city of refuge before his trial. The Torah states that an unintentional murderer is required to remain in the city of refuge to which he fled until the death of the High Priest. The mishna elaborates: With regard to High Priests, who were appointed in several different manners,

chunks.en: A Kohen Gadol anointed with the special oil,
chunks.st: one anointed with the anointing oil,
chunks.stMore: which was the method through which High Priests were consecrated until the oil was sequestered toward the end of the First Temple period;

chunks.en: or one who wears the extra special clothes,
chunks.explain: The eight special clothes of the Kohen Gadol.
chunks.st: and one consecrated by donning multiple garments,
chunks.stMore: the eight vestments unique to the High Priest, which was the practice during the Second Temple period;

chunks.en: or one who was a Kohen Gadol for a while and stepped down,
chunks.st: and one who received a temporary appointment due to the unfitness of the serving High Priest, who departed from his anointment
chunks.stMore: with the restoration of the serving High Priest to active service,

chunks.en: when they die, the killer goes back home.
chunks.st: their deaths facilitate the return of the murderer
chunks.stMore: from the city of refuge to his home.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.he: אַף מְשׁוּחַ מִלְחָמָה מַחֲזִיר אֶת הָרוֹצֵחַ.
chunks.en: Even the Kohen anointed for war sends the killer back home.
chunks.st: Even the death of a priest anointed for war to address the soldiers (see Deuteronomy 20:1–7) facilitates the return of the murderer.

chunks.en: So the mothers of the Kohanim Gedolim
chunks.st: The mishna continues: Therefore, the mothers of High Priests

chunks.en: give food and clothing to the people in galus,
chunks.st: would provide those exiled to cities of refuge with sustenance and garments

chunks.he: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִתְפַּלְּלוּ עַל בְּנֵיהֶם שֶׁיָּמוּתוּ.
chunks.en: so that they will not daven that their sons should die.
chunks.st: so that they would not pray that their sons would die.
chunks.stMore: The more comfortable their lives in the city of refuge, the less urgency they would feel to leave, and the less likely it would be that they would pray for the death of the High Priests.

chunks.en: If after his judgment was decided, the Kohen Gadol died,
chunks.st: If, after the unintentional murderer’s verdict was decided and he was sentenced to exile, the High Priest died,

chunks.en: he does not go into galus.
chunks.st: he is not exiled,
chunks.stMore: as the death of the High Priest exempts him from exile.

chunks.en: If before his judgment was decided,
chunks.st: If it was before his verdict was decided

chunks.he: מֵת כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וּמִנּוּ אַחֵר תַּחְתָּיו,
chunks.en: the Kohen Gadol died and they chose another in his place,
chunks.st: that the High Priest died and they appointed another in his place,

chunks.en: and after that his judgment was decided,
chunks.st: and thereafter his verdict was decided,

chunks.en: he goes home when the second one dies.
chunks.st: he returns from exile with the death of the second High Priest.

mishnayos.summary: In some cases the one in galus can never leave the city of refuge, not even to be a witness or to help the Jewish people. The mishnah also teaches about the area around the city, and what happens if he leaves it.

chunks.en: If his judgment was decided when there was no Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: If the verdict of a murderer was decided at a time when there was no High Priest,

chunks.en: or he killed a Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: and likewise in the cases of one who unintentionally killed a High Priest

chunks.en: or he is a Kohen Gadol who killed,
chunks.st: and in the case of a High Priest who killed unintentionally,

chunks.en: he never leaves there.
chunks.st: the unintentional murderer never leaves the city of refuge.

chunks.en: And he does not leave to be a witness for a mitzvah,
chunks.st: And one who is exiled may not leave the city at all, either for testimony relating to a mitzva,

chunks.en: or to be a witness about money,
chunks.st: or for testimony relating to monetary matters,

chunks.en: or to be a witness in a case of life and death.
chunks.st: or for testimony relating to capital matters.

chunks.en: And even if the Jewish people need him,
chunks.st: And even if the Jewish people require his services,

chunks.en: and even if he is the general of the army of Yisrael
chunks.st: and even if he is the general of the army of Israel

chunks.en: like Yoav ben Tzeruyah,
chunks.st: like Joab ben Zeruiah,

words.note: King Dovid's general.

chunks.en: he never leaves there,
chunks.st: he never leaves the city of refuge,

chunks.en: as it says, "where he ran away to."
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And the congregation shall restore him to his city of refuge, that he fled there”
chunks.stMore: (Numbers 35:25), from which it is derived:

chunks.en: There he shall live,
chunks.st: There shall be his dwelling,

chunks.en: there he shall pass away,
chunks.st: there shall be his death,

chunks.en: there he shall be buried.
chunks.st: there shall be his burial.
chunks.stMore: The mishna continues:

chunks.en: Just as the city protects him,
chunks.st: Just as an unintentional murderer is admitted to the city of refuge,

chunks.en: so does the area around it protect him.
chunks.st: so is he admitted to its outskirts, located within the Shabbat boundary.
chunks.stMore: Once he entered the outskirts of the city, the blood redeemer may not kill him.

words.note: The area around the city, up to the Shabbos boundary.

chunks.en: If the killer went out past the boundary
chunks.st: In a case where a murderer emerged beyond the Shabbat boundary of the city of refuge

chunks.en: and the go'el hadam found him,
chunks.st: and the blood redeemer found him there,

words.note: The go'el hadam, a relative of the one who was killed.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:

chunks.en: it is a mitzvah for the go'el hadam to kill him,
chunks.st: It is a mitzva for the blood redeemer to kill him,

chunks.en: and anyone else is allowed to.
chunks.st: and it is optional for every other person to do so.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: The go'el hadam is allowed to,
chunks.st: It is optional for the blood redeemer,

chunks.en: but anyone else is punished for it.
chunks.st: and every other person is liable for killing him.
chunks.stMore: The previous mishna teaches that the halakhic status of the outskirts of the city is like that of the city itself in terms of the unintentional murderer being provided refuge there. The mishna adds:

chunks.en: A tree that stands inside the boundary
chunks.st: With regard to a tree that stands within the Shabbat boundary of a city of refuge,

chunks.en: with its branches leaning outside the boundary,
chunks.st: whose boughs extend outside the boundary,

chunks.en: or it stands outside the boundary
chunks.st: or a tree that stands outside the boundary

chunks.en: with its branches leaning inside the boundary:
chunks.st: and its boughs extend inside the boundary,

chunks.en: it all follows the branches.
chunks.st: the status of the tree, whether it is considered inside or outside the boundary, in all cases follows the boughs.

chunks.en: If he killed by accident in that same city,
chunks.st: If an unintentional murderer, exiled to a city of refuge, unintentionally killed a person in the same city,

chunks.en: he moves from one neighborhood to another.
chunks.st: he is exiled from that neighborhood where he resided to another neighborhood within that city.

chunks.en: And a Levi who lives there
chunks.st: And a Levite who is a permanent resident of a city of refuge and unintentionally killed a person

chunks.en: moves from one city to another.
chunks.st: is exiled from that city to another city.

mishnayos.summary: The one in galus must tell people why he is there, but he may accept their honor. The Tannaim argue whether he paid rent to the Leviim, and whether he gets back his old job when he goes home.

chunks.en: Similarly,
chunks.st: Similarly,

chunks.en: a killer who went into galus to his city of refuge,
chunks.st: in the case of a murderer who was exiled to a city of refuge

chunks.en: and the people of the city wanted to honor him,
chunks.st: and the people of the city sought to honor him due to his prominence,

chunks.en: he should tell them, "I killed someone."
chunks.st: he shall say to them: I am a murderer.

chunks.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ אַף עַל פִּי כֵן,
chunks.en: If they say to him, "Even so,"
chunks.st: If the residents of the city say to him: We are aware of your status and nevertheless, we wish to honor you,

chunks.en: he may accept it from them,
chunks.st: he may accept the honor from them,

chunks.en: as it says, "And this is the word of the killer."
chunks.explain: He only needs to say it once.
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And this is the matter [devar] of the murderer” (Deuteronomy 19:4),
chunks.stMore: from which it is derived that the murderer is required to say [ledabber] to them that he is a murderer. He is not required to tell them any more than that.

chunks.en: They would pay rent to the Leviim,
chunks.explain: The cities of refuge belonged to the Leviim.
chunks.st: The unintentional murderers would pay a fee to the Levites
chunks.stMore: as rent for their living quarters in the cities of refuge, which were Levite cities;

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: They did not pay them rent.
chunks.st: They would not pay a fee to them,
chunks.stMore: but would reside rent free, as they are required to live there by Torah law. They also disagreed with regard to the status of the unintentional murderer when he returns home after the death of the High Priest.

chunks.en: And he goes back to the important job he had before,
chunks.st: He returns to the same public office that he occupied prior to his exile;

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.he: לֹא הָיָה חוֹזֵר לַשְּׂרָרָה שֶׁהָיָה בָהּ:
chunks.en: He does not go back to the important job he had.
chunks.st: He does not return to the office that he occupied.

mishnayos.summary: Now the mishnah lists people who get lashes. First are those who have a forbidden relationship with certain relatives, and Kohanim or others who marry someone the Torah does not allow them to marry.

chunks.en: And these are the ones who get lashes:
one who has a forbidden relationship with his sister,

words.note: Has a forbidden relationship.

chunks.en: or his father's sister,
or his mother's sister,
or his wife's sister,
or his brother's wife,
or his father's brother's wife,
or a niddah.
Also a widow who marries a Kohen Gadol,
a divorced woman or a chalutzah who marries a regular Kohen,
a mamzeres or a nesinah who marries a regular Jew,

words.note: A girl born from a forbidden relationship.
From the Givonim, who may not marry into the Jewish people.

chunks.en: or a Jewish girl who marries a nasin or a mamzer.
If she is a widow and also divorced,
a Kohen Gadol who marries her gets lashes for two different aveiros.
If she is divorced and also a chalutzah,

chunks.he: אֵינוֹ חַיָּב אֶלָּא מִשֵּׁם אֶחָד בִּלְבָד:
chunks.en: a regular Kohen who marries her is punished for only one aveirah.

mishnayos.summary: More people who get lashes: for eating holy food while tamei, eating forbidden foods like cheilev, blood, chametz on Pesach, and untithed food, and for doing other aveiros. Rabbi Shimon and the Sages argue how much tevel one must eat to get lashes.

chunks.en: A tamei person who ate holy food from a korban,
chunks.st: A ritually impure person who ate sacrificial food

chunks.en: and one who came into the Beis HaMikdash while tamei,
chunks.st: and one who entered the Temple while ritually impure.

chunks.en: and one who eats cheilev,
chunks.st: And one who eats the forbidden fat of a domesticated animal;

words.note: Fat of an animal that the Torah forbids.

chunks.en: or blood, or nossar,
chunks.st: or blood; or notar,
chunks.stMore: leftover flesh from an offering after the time allotted for its consumption;

words.note: Meat of a korban left over after its time.

chunks.en: or piggul,
chunks.explain: A korban ruined by a wrong plan while bringing it.
chunks.st: or piggul,
chunks.stMore: an offering invalidated due to intent to sprinkle its blood, burn its fats on the altar, or consume it, beyond its designated time;

chunks.en: or a korban that became tamei,
chunks.st: or one who partakes of an offering that became impure, is flogged.

chunks.en: one who shechts or brings a korban outside the Beis HaMikdash,
chunks.st: And one who slaughters a sacrificial animal or sacrifices it on an altar outside the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: and one who eats chametz on Pesach,
chunks.st: and one who eats leavened bread on Passover,

chunks.en: and one who eats or does melachah on Yom Kippur,
chunks.st: and one who eats on Yom Kippur and one who performs labor on Yom Kippur,

chunks.en: and one who mixes the special anointing oil for himself,
chunks.st: and one who blends the anointing oil for non-sacred use,

chunks.en: and one who mixes the ketores for himself,
chunks.st: and one who blends the incense that was burned on the altar in the Sanctuary for non-sacred use,

words.note: The special incense burned in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: and one who smears himself with the anointing oil,
chunks.st: and one who applies the anointing oil,

chunks.en: and one who eats neveilos and treifos,
chunks.st: and one who eats unslaughtered animal or bird carcasses, or tereifot,
chunks.stMore: which are animals or birds with a condition that will lead to their death within twelve months,

words.note: Animals that died without shechitah.
Animals with a deadly injury or sickness.

chunks.en: or creepy crawly creatures.
chunks.st: or repugnant creatures, or creeping animals,
chunks.stMore: is liable to receive lashes.

words.note: Disgusting creatures, like bugs.
Creeping creatures.

chunks.en: If he ate tevel, or ma'aser rishon
chunks.st: If one ate untithed produce,
chunks.stMore: i.e., produce from which terumot and tithes were not separated;

words.note: Food that terumah and ma'aser were not yet taken from.
The first tithe, given to a Levi.

chunks.en: whose terumah was not taken from it,
chunks.st: or first-tithe produce whose teruma of the tithe was not taken;

chunks.en: or ma'aser sheni or hekdesh that was not redeemed,
chunks.st: or second-tithe produce or sacrificial food that was not redeemed;
chunks.stMore: he is liable to receive lashes. With regard to the measure for liability for eating forbidden food, the mishna asks:

words.note: The second tithe, eaten in Yerushalayim.
Something given to the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.he: כַּמָּה יֹאכַל מִן הַטֶּבֶל וִיהֵא חַיָּב,
chunks.en: How much tevel must one eat to get lashes?
chunks.st: How much does one need to eat from untithed produce and be liable to receive lashes?

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says, any amount.
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says: If one ate any amount
chunks.stMore: of untithed produce he is liable to receive lashes.

chunks.en: But the Sages say, a kezayis.
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say: He is liable only if he eats an olive-bulk,
chunks.stMore: which is the minimum measure characterized as eating.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon said to them,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon said to them:

chunks.en: Don't you agree with me that
chunks.st: Do you not concede to me

chunks.en: one who eats an ant of any size is punished?
chunks.st: with regard to one who eats an ant of any size that he is liable to receive lashes?

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to Rabbi Shimon:

chunks.en: That is because it is a whole creature, the way Hashem made it.
chunks.st: He receives lashes for eating an ant of any size due to the fact that it is an intact entity in the form of its creation,
chunks.stMore: and that is what the Torah prohibited.

chunks.en: He said to them,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon said to them:

chunks.en: One kernel of wheat is also whole, the way Hashem made it!
chunks.st: One kernel of wheat is also in the form of its creation, and therefore one should be liable to receive lashes for eating any intact entity.

mishnayos.stIntro: The mishna continues enumerating those liable to receive lashes:

mishnayos.summary: More people who get forty lashes: eating holy food at the wrong time or in the wrong place, and breaking a bone of the korban Pesach.

chunks.he: הָאוֹכֵל בִּכּוּרִים עַד שֶׁלֹּא קָרָא עֲלֵיהֶן,
chunks.en: One who eats bikkurim before the owner said the special words over them,
chunks.explain: Bikkurim are the first fruits brought to the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: In the case of a priest who eats first fruits before the one who brought the fruits to the Temple recited over those fruits the Torah verses that he is obligated to recite (see Deuteronomy 26:3–10);

chunks.en: or the holiest korbanos outside the curtains of the courtyard,
chunks.st: and one who ate offerings of the most sacred order outside the curtains surrounding the Tabernacle courtyard, or outside the Temple courtyard;

chunks.he: קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי חוּץ לַחוֹמָה,
chunks.en: or less-holy korbanos or ma'aser sheni outside the wall of Yerushalayim,
chunks.st: and one who ate offerings of lesser sanctity or second-tithe produce outside the wall of Jerusalem;

chunks.en: or one who breaks a bone of a tahor korban Pesach,
chunks.st: and also one who breaks the bone of a ritually pure Paschal offering;

chunks.en: gets forty lashes.
chunks.st: in all these cases he is flogged with forty lashes.

chunks.en: But one who leaves over meat of a tahor Pesach, or breaks a bone of a tamei one,
chunks.st: But one who leaves the flesh of the ritually pure Paschal offering until the morning of the fifteenth of Nisan, and one who breaks a bone of a ritually impure Paschal offering,

chunks.en: does not get forty lashes.
chunks.st: is not flogged with forty lashes.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who takes a mother bird together with her babies: Rabbi Yehuda says he gets lashes. The Sages say he sends away the mother and does not get lashes, because the aveirah can be fixed by doing a mitzvah.

chunks.en: One who takes a mother bird with her babies,
chunks.st: With regard to one who takes the mother bird with her fledglings,
chunks.stMore: thereby violating the Torah prohibition: “You shall not take the mother with her fledglings; you shall send the mother, and the fledglings you may take for yourself” (Deuteronomy 22:6–7),

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: He gets lashes and does not send away the mother.
chunks.st: He is flogged for taking the mother bird, and does not send the mother,

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: and the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: He sends away the mother and does not get lashes.
chunks.st: He sends the mother and is not flogged,

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: as this is the principle:

chunks.en: Any "do not" mitzvah
chunks.st: With regard to any prohibition

chunks.en: that has a mitzvah to get up and do something to fix it,
chunks.st: that entails a command to arise and perform a mitzva,

chunks.en: one does not get lashes for it.
chunks.st: he is not liable to receive lashes for its violation.

mishnayos.summary: More people who get lashes: one who makes a bald spot, shaves the corners of his head or beard, or makes a cut on his skin for someone who died. Each one counts separately.

chunks.en: One who makes a bald spot on his head,
chunks.explain: As a sign of sadness for someone who passed away.
chunks.st: One who creates a bald spot upon his head,

chunks.en: and one who shaves around the corner of his head,
chunks.st: and one who rounds the edge of his head
chunks.stMore: by shaving the hair adjacent to the ear,

chunks.en: and one who ruins the corner of his beard,
chunks.st: and one who mars the edge of his beard,

chunks.en: and one who makes one cut on his skin for someone who died,
chunks.st: and one who cuts one incision in a display of mourning over the dead,

chunks.en: gets lashes.
chunks.st: are all liable to receive lashes.

chunks.he: שָׂרַט שְׂרִיטָה אַחַת עַל חֲמִשָּׁה מֵתִים
chunks.en: If he made one cut for five people who died,
chunks.st: If he cut one incision over five dead people,

chunks.he: אוֹ חָמֵשׁ שְׂרִיטוֹת עַל מֵת אֶחָד,
chunks.en: or five cuts for one person,
chunks.st: or five incisions over one dead person,

chunks.en: he is punished for each and every one.
chunks.st: he is liable to receive lashes for each and every one.

chunks.en: For the head,
chunks.st: For rounding the edges of his head,

chunks.en: there are two corners: one on this side and one on that side.
chunks.st: one is liable to receive two sets of lashes, one from here, the hair adjacent to one ear, and one from there, the hair adjacent to the other ear.

chunks.en: For the beard,
chunks.st: For marring the edges of his beard

chunks.he: שְׁתַּיִם מִכָּאן וּשְׁתַּיִם מִכָּאן וְאַחַת מִלְּמָטָּה.
chunks.en: there are two on this side, two on that side, and one below.
chunks.st: there are two edges from here, on one side of his face, and two from there, on the other side, and one from below, on his chin.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: If he took it all off at once,
chunks.st: If he removed the hair on all the edges of his beard in one action,

chunks.en: he is punished only once.
chunks.st: he is liable to receive only one set of lashes for all of them.

chunks.en: And he is punished only if he takes it off with a razor.
chunks.st: And one is liable for marring the edges of his beard only if he removes the hair with a razor.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.he: אֲפִלּוּ לִקְּטוֹ בְמַלְקֵט אוֹ בִרְהִיטְנִי, חַיָּב:
chunks.en: Even if he pulled it out with tweezers or a scraper, he is punished.
chunks.st: Even if he removed the hair with tweezers [malket] or with a plane [rehitni], he is liable to receive lashes.

mishnayos.summary: One who makes a tattoo gets lashes, but only if he both scratches the skin and puts in ink. Rabbi Shimon says only if he writes a name there.

chunks.en: One who writes a tattoo,
chunks.st: One who imprints a tattoo, by inserting a dye into recesses carved in the skin, is also liable to receive lashes.

chunks.en: if he wrote with ink but did not scratch the skin,
chunks.st: If one imprinted on the skin with a dye but did not carve the skin,

chunks.en: or he scratched the skin but did not put in ink,
chunks.st: or if one carved the skin but did not imprint the tattoo by adding a dye,

chunks.en: he is not punished,
chunks.st: he is not liable;

chunks.en: until he writes and scratches, with ink or with kochol,
chunks.st: he is not liable until he imprints and carves the skin, with ink, or with kohl [keḥol],

words.note: A dark paint for the eyes.

chunks.en: or with anything that leaves a mark.
chunks.st: or with any substance that marks.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda

chunks.en: says in the name of Rabbi Shimon,
chunks.st: says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:

chunks.he: אֵינוֹ חַיָּב עַד שֶׁיִּכְתּוֹב שָׁם הַשֵּׁם,
chunks.en: He is punished only if he writes the name of an idol there,
chunks.st: He is liable only if he writes the name there,
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura explains that it means the name of an idol.

chunks.en: as it says, "Do not put a tattoo
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And a tattoo inscription

chunks.en: on yourselves; I am Hashem."
chunks.st: you shall not place upon you, I am the Lord” (Leviticus 19:28).

mishnayos.summary: A nazir who drinks wine all day gets only one set of lashes. But if people keep warning him and he keeps drinking, he is punished for each time.

chunks.he: נָזִיר שֶׁהָיָה שׁוֹתֶה בַיַּיִן כָּל הַיּוֹם,
chunks.en: A nazir who was drinking wine all day
chunks.st: A nazirite who was drinking wine all day

words.note: Someone who promised not to drink wine, cut his hair, or become tamei from the dead.

chunks.en: is punished only once.
chunks.st: is liable to receive only one set of lashes.

chunks.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ אַל תִּשְׁתֶּה אַל תִּשְׁתֶּה
chunks.en: If they said to him, "Don't drink! Don't drink!"
chunks.st: If onlookers said to him: Do not drink, do not drink,

chunks.en: and he keeps drinking,
chunks.st: forewarning him several times, and he drinks after each forewarning,

chunks.en: he is punished for each and every time.
chunks.st: he is liable to receive lashes for each and every drink.

mishnayos.summary: The same is true for a nazir who becomes tamei from the dead or shaves, and for anyone who wears sha'atnez: if they keep warning him and he keeps doing it, he is punished for each time.

chunks.en: If a nazir kept becoming tamei from the dead all day,
chunks.st: If the nazirite was rendering himself impure through exposure to corpses all day,

chunks.en: he is punished only once.
chunks.st: he is liable to receive only one set of lashes.

chunks.en: If they said to him, "Don't become tamei!
chunks.st: If they said to him: Do not render yourself impure,

chunks.en: Don't become tamei!"
chunks.st: do not render yourself impure,

chunks.en: and he kept becoming tamei,
chunks.st: and he renders himself impure after each forewarning,

chunks.en: he is punished for each and every time.
chunks.st: he is liable for each and every incident.

chunks.en: If he was shaving all day,
chunks.st: If the nazirite was shaving his hair all day,

chunks.en: he is punished only once.
chunks.st: he is liable to receive only one set of lashes.

chunks.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ אַל תְּגַלֵּחַ אַל תְּגַלֵּחַ
chunks.en: If they said to him, "Don't shave! Don't shave!"
chunks.st: If they said to him: Do not shave, do not shave,

chunks.en: and he keeps shaving,
chunks.st: and after each forewarning he shaves,

chunks.en: he is punished for each and every time.
chunks.st: he is liable for each and every time he shaves.

chunks.en: If someone was wearing sha'atnez all day,
chunks.explain: Sha'atnez is cloth of wool and linen mixed together.
chunks.st: If a person was wearing a garment consisting of diverse kinds of wool and linen all day,

words.note: Sha'atnez, wool and linen together.

chunks.en: he is punished only once.
chunks.st: he is liable to receive only one set of lashes.

chunks.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ אַל תִּלְבָּשׁ אַל תִּלְבָּשׁ
chunks.en: If they said to him, "Don't wear it! Don't wear it!"
chunks.st: If they said to him: Do not wear it, do not wear it,

chunks.en: and he takes it off and puts it on again,
chunks.st: and he removes it and dons it after each forewarning,

chunks.en: he is punished for each and every time.
chunks.st: he is liable for each and every time that he dons the garment.

mishnayos.summary: With one furrow of plowing, a person can break eight "do not" mitzvos at once! The mishnah lists them, and Chananya ben Chachinai adds wearing sha'atnez.

chunks.en: There is someone who plows one furrow
chunks.st: There is one who plows a single furrow

chunks.en: and is punished for eight "do not" mitzvos:
chunks.st: and is liable to receive lashes for violating eight prohibitions.
chunks.stMore: How so?

chunks.en: one who plows with an ox and a donkey together,
chunks.st: For plowing with an ox and a donkey, in violation of the prohibition: “You shall not plow with an ox and a donkey together” (Deuteronomy 22:10);

chunks.en: and they belong to the Beis HaMikdash,
chunks.st: and they are consecrated, and therefore he is guilty of misuse of consecrated property;

chunks.en: planting kilayim in a vineyard,
chunks.explain: Kilayim means mixing seeds of different kinds.
chunks.st: and he is plowing diverse kinds in a vineyard;

chunks.en: in the Shemittah year, on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: and it is during the Sabbatical Year, when it is prohibited to work the land; and it is on a Festival, when plowing is a prohibited labor;

chunks.en: and he is a Kohen and a nazir in a place that is tamei from the dead.
chunks.st: and he is both a priest and a nazirite and is performing the plowing in a place of impurity imparted by a corpse, which is prohibited for both a priest (see Leviticus 21:1) and a nazirite (see Numbers 6:6).

chunks.en: Chananya ben Chachinai says,
chunks.st: Ḥananya ben Ḥakhinai says:

chunks.en: Also if he was wearing sha'atnez.
chunks.st: If he was wearing a garment consisting of diverse kinds of wool and linen while plowing he is also flogged for violating that prohibition.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The Sages said to him:

chunks.en: That is not the same kind.
chunks.explain: It has nothing to do with plowing.
chunks.st: That is not a prohibition in the same category as the others, as it is not connected to the act of plowing.

chunks.en: He said to them,
chunks.st: Ḥananya ben Ḥakhinai said to them:

chunks.en: Being a nazir is also not the same kind!
chunks.st: According to that criterion, the fact that he is a nazirite is also not in the same category, as a nazirite and a priest are not flogged for plowing; rather, they are flogged for contracting impurity imparted by a corpse.

mishnayos.stIntro: Apropos the case where one receives several sets of lashes for performing a single action, the mishna continues:

mishnayos.summary: Malkus is thirty-nine lashes, not forty, because of how the pasuk is read. Rabbi Yehuda says it is a full forty.

chunks.en: How many lashes do they give him?
chunks.st: With how many lashes does one flog a person sentenced to receive lashes?

chunks.en: Forty minus one.
chunks.st: One flogs him with forty lashes less one,

chunks.en: As it says, "by number, forty,"
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And he shall strike him before him, in accordance with his wickedness, by number. Forty he shall strike him, he shall not add” (Deuteronomy 25:2–3).
chunks.stMore: The mishna joins the end of the first verse and the beginning of the second, forming the phrase: “By number, forty,” which is interpreted as:

chunks.en: meaning a number that is close to forty.
chunks.st: A sum adjacent to forty.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: He gets a full forty.
chunks.st: He is flogged with a full forty lashes.

chunks.en: And where does he get the extra one?
chunks.st: And where is he flogged the extra lash?
chunks.stMore: As the mishna proceeds to explain, the thirty-nine lashes are divided into three and administered in three places on the body of the person being flogged; according to Rabbi Yehuda there is one lash that remains.

chunks.en: Between his shoulders.
chunks.st: That lash is administered between his shoulders.

mishnayos.summary: Beis Din checks how many lashes a person can safely take, always a number that splits into three. If he cannot take more, he is let go.

chunks.en: They only decide how many he can take
chunks.st: One assesses the number of lashes that the one being punished is capable of withstanding only with

chunks.en: using a number that can be split into three.
chunks.explain: Like eighteen, which is three sixes.
chunks.st: a number of lashes fit to be divided into three equal groups.
chunks.stMore: If the assessment was that he can survive twenty lashes, he is flogged with eighteen.

chunks.en: If they decided he can take forty,
chunks.st: Likewise, if doctors assessed concerning him that he is able to receive forty lashes and survive,

chunks.en: and after he got some lashes,
chunks.st: and he is then flogged some of those forty lashes,

chunks.en: they said he cannot take forty,
chunks.st: and then they assessed him again and concluded that he cannot receive forty lashes and survive,

chunks.en: he is free from the rest.
chunks.st: he is exempt from the additional lashes.

chunks.en: If they decided he can take eighteen,
chunks.st: If the doctors initially assessed concerning him that he is able to receive only eighteen lashes,

chunks.he: מִשֶּׁלָּקָה אָמְרוּ שֶׁיָּכוֹל הוּא לְקַבֵּל אַרְבָּעִים,
chunks.en: and after he got them, they said he can take forty,
chunks.st: and once he was flogged eighteen times they assessed that he is able to receive forty,

chunks.en: he is free.
chunks.st: he is exempt from receiving additional lashes.

chunks.he: עָבַר עֲבֵרָה שֶׁיֶּשׁ בָּהּ שְׁנֵי לָאוִין,
chunks.en: If he did an aveirah that breaks two "do not" mitzvos,
chunks.st: If one performed a transgression that involves two prohibitions,

chunks.en: and they made one estimate for both,
chunks.st: and they assessed concerning him a single assessment
chunks.stMore: of the number of lashes that he could withstand in punishment for both transgressions,

chunks.en: he gets those lashes and is free.
chunks.st: he is flogged in accordance with their assessment and is exempt from any additional lashes.

chunks.en: But if not,
chunks.st: And if not,
chunks.stMore: if he was assessed with regard to the lashes that he could withstand for one transgression,

chunks.en: he gets lashes, heals, and then gets lashes again.
chunks.st: he is flogged and is allowed to heal, and then is flogged again for violating the second prohibition.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah begins to describe how Beis Din gave lashes, with the shamash of Beis Din standing on a stone and holding a strap.

chunks.en: How do they give him lashes?
They tie his two hands to
a post, on each side.
The shamash takes hold of his clothes.
If they tear, they tear,
and if they come apart, they come apart,
until his chest is uncovered.
A stone is placed behind him,
and the shamash stands on it,
with a strap of calf leather in his hand,
folded, one into two and two into four,
and two straps of donkey leather go up and down on it.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah tells the size of the strap and how the lashes were given: one third in front and two thirds behind, while the person is bent over.

chunks.en: Its handle is a tefach long, and it is a tefach wide,

words.note: About the width of a hand.

chunks.en: and its end reaches the top of his belly.
He gives him one third of the lashes in front
and two thirds behind.
He does not hit him while he is standing
or sitting, but while he is bent over,
as it says, "The judge shall make him lie down."

words.en: and he shall make him lie down

chunks.he: וְהַמַּכֶּה מַכֶּה בְיָדוֹ אַחַת בְּכָל כֹּחוֹ:
chunks.en: And the one giving the lashes hits with one hand, with all his strength.

mishnayos.summary: While the lashes are given, pesukim are read aloud, ending with "He is merciful and forgives sin." The mishnah also teaches when the shamash is punished and when the lashes are stopped.

chunks.en: And the reader reads, "If you do not

chunks.he: תִשְׁמֹר לַעֲשׂוֹת וְגוֹ' וְהִפְלָא ה' אֶת
chunks.en: keep and do... then Hashem will make
your punishments great, and the punishments..."
Then he goes back to the start of the pasuk. Then he reads, "And you shall keep
the words of this covenant..."
And he ends with, "And He is merciful,
He forgives sin...",
and goes back to the start of the pasuk.
If the person dies from the lashes,
the shamash is not punished.
chunks.explain: He did what Beis Din told him.

chunks.he: הוֹסִיף לוֹ עוֹד רְצוּעָה אַחַת וָמֵת,
chunks.en: If he gave him one extra lash and he died,
the shamash goes into galus because of him.
If he dirtied himself, in either way,
chunks.explain: Because he was afraid.

chunks.en: he is free from more lashes.
Rabbi Yehuda says,
A man only with the first kind, and a woman even with the second.

mishnayos.summary: Getting lashes takes away the punishment of kares. The Tannaim teach how great the reward is for doing a mitzvah, and even for holding back from an aveirah.

chunks.en: All those who deserve kares and got lashes

words.note: Being cut off, a punishment from Hashem.

chunks.en: are freed from their kares,
as it says, "And your brother will be shamed before your eyes."
Once he got lashes, he is like your brother again.
These are the words of Rabbi Chananya ben Gamliel.
Rabbi Chananya ben Gamliel said,
If someone who does one aveirah
loses his soul for it,
then someone who does one mitzvah,
how much more so
will his soul be given to him!
Rabbi Shimon says,
We learn it from the same place,
as it says, "And they shall be cut off,

words.en: and they shall be cut off

chunks.en: the souls that do these..."
and it says, "Which a person shall do
and live by them."

chunks.he: הָא, כָּל הַיּוֹשֵׁב וְלֹא עָבַר עֲבֵרָה,
chunks.en: So anyone who sits and does not do an aveirah
gets a reward like someone who does a mitzvah.
Rabbi Shimon the son of Rebbi says,
The pasuk says,
"Only be strong not to eat the blood,
for the blood is the soul."
If blood, which a person's soul
finds disgusting,
gets a reward for staying away from it,
then stealing and forbidden relationships, which a person's soul
wants and craves,
one who stays away from them,
how much more so
will he earn a reward, for himself and his children,

chunks.he: וּלְדוֹרוֹת דּוֹרוֹתָיו עַד סוֹף כָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת:
chunks.en: and for their children, until the end of all the generations!

mishnayos.summary: Hashem wanted to give the Jewish people many chances to earn merit, so He gave them lots of Torah and mitzvos.

chunks.en: Rabbi Chananya ben Akashya says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Ḥananya ben Akashya says:

chunks.en: Hakadosh Baruch Hu wanted
chunks.st: The Holy One, Blessed be He,

chunks.en: to give merit to Yisrael,
chunks.st: sought to confer merit upon the Jewish people;

chunks.en: so He gave them lots of Torah and mitzvos,
chunks.st: therefore, He increased for them Torah and mitzvot, as each mitzva increases merit,

chunks.en: as it says, "Hashem wanted,
chunks.st: as it is stated: “It pleased the Lord

chunks.en: for the sake of His righteousness, to make the Torah great and glorious."
chunks.st: for the sake of His righteousness to make the Torah great and glorious” (Isaiah 42:21). God sought to make the Torah great and glorious by means of the proliferation of mitzvot.
